section: note
Item: BLUF: (1) The workbook contains no '~$10B/yr' figure; its cost anchors are $21.4M/yr per dedicated vessel, $9.3M/yr per piggyback ship and $175B-$18T/yr for 1 K of global cooling. (2) Its nozzle power (512 W) and output (1.73e12 particles/s) match the Harrison et al. 2025 paper held in precis, but the 150 nm design size is not what that nozzle makes (count median 49.5 nm). (3) Its tonnage-per-K spread (31x) comes from a J. Climate paper that is a stub in precis; the full-text preprint by the same group gives 13x for equal forcing. (4) The damage-per-K band (0.6/3.3/12 % of GDP) rests on sources with no text in precis. (5) The two 2026 EU storm events (about USD 7.0B insured, hand-converted) are 329 dedicated vessel-years or 761 piggyback ship-years of Tito's cost, and 0.04%-4.0% of his per-K annual cost; hail and AMOC bear on the benefit side only as a scale cross-check and a model-dependent caveat.

Item: Limits of this comparison: two events in one season are not an annual loss; insured loss is below economic loss; PERILS estimates are provisional (updates follow); and no source in precis says how much of this hail loss 1 K of marine cloud brightening would avoid (Perplexity: share of hail loss that scales with temperature 'Not sourced'). section: Flag legend
Item: stub = source paper/report has no full text in precis; perplexity-only = only source is a Perplexity ref; hand-FX = currency conversion done by hand with the ECB rate (date and rate recorded); unverified = quote not found in source text; no-source = cell left empty; verified = value and quote read in text held in precis (or arithmetic on such values). Workbook cell values were read from the file with a data-only loader.
